WindowRef.$doc: A top-level window. handle is the HWND as a decimal string (JS numbers cannot hold 64-bit values).
WindowRef.title: string

elevated.doc: The window's process runs elevated: the shell (not elevated) cannot activate/minimise/close it (UIPI). UI shows a hint.

id.doc: Pinned id or running app id (see PinnedItem.id); separators use 'separator:N'.

badge.doc: Reserved: always null on Windows (no API exposes taskbar overlay badges to other processes).

windows.doc: Windows of this app, most recently active first.

launching.doc: Launch requested but no window yet. The host adds a transient item for unpinned apps and removes it on the first window or after 20 s.

items.doc: Pinned items in user order, then running-but-unpinned apps; folders and the trash-like tail after a separator.

itemIds.doc: Full ordered list of PINNED item ids.

thumbUrl.doc: https://app.local/dyn/thumb/<handle>?w=<px>&rev=<n>; may be absent until captured (then mc.thumbnail fires).

monitorId.doc: Monitor whose area contains the window's centre.
null = the overlay's monitor. Only windows whose centre lies on this monitor are returned; bounds are DIPs relative to this monitor's top-left (converted with its scale).

path.doc: Absolute path of a folder, exe or lnk to pin (the UI obtains it with system.pickPath).

activeApp.changed.doc: Foreground app (ignoring BetterWindows' own windows). Drives the menu bar app name.

dock.state.doc: Full dock model; pushed on any window/pin/settings change (coalesced to >=50 ms).

dock.reveal.doc: Auto-hide: host detected the pointer at the dock edge (true) or leaving (false).

mc.thumbnail.doc: A thumbnail became available after mc.snapshot.

mc.changed.doc: Pushed to the overlay while mode=missionControl is shown whenever windows or desktops change (coalesced >= 100 ms). mc.thumbnail still fills in thumbnails.

dock.activate.doc: Launch if not running; else focus the most recent window (restore if minimised); folders open in Explorer.

dock.pin.doc: Pin by app id (from the catalog or a running app). index = position in settings.dock.pins; folders are always appended after apps.

dock.quit.doc: Close all windows of the app (WM_CLOSE). itemId may be ANY running app id, not only a visible dock item (used by the app menu).

dock.hide.doc: Minimise all windows of the app. itemId may be ANY running app id (used by the app menu).

dock.pinPath.doc: Pin a folder / exe / lnk by path (folders become kind=folder items, exe/lnk become app items with id exe:<path>).
